name: FloodDiffusion 2
summary: Open-source streaming text-to-motion model from AlayaLab: generates continuous 3D human motion from changing text prompts, with root-path control of the trajectory. KV-cached partial attention gives ~2.3 ms/step on an RTX 4090 per the authors. Code, checkpoints, prepared datasets and a live HF demo are public.

access.license: MIT (code); checkpoints carry no license tag
access.notes: Code MIT. HF checkpoints have no explicit license; trained on HumanML3D/BABEL/SEED, which keep their own terms. Mesh rendering needs SMPL-H from mano.is.tue.mpg.de (separate license, not bundled).

procedure: git clone https://github.com/AlayaLab/FloodDiffusion2 and create a Python 3.10 env
Run python setup_project.py: installs deps and downloads the four paper checkpoints plus UMT5/T2M/GloVe assets from Hugging Face
Optional: --with-data for prepared datasets, --smplh <path> to import a licensed SMPL-H model for mesh rendering
Or try it in the browser: https://huggingface.co/spaces/AlayaLab/FloodDiffusion2-Live

stats.size: Inference tested on RTX 4090; Linux + NVIDIA recommended

verdict.why: Real, complete release (code, weights, data, demo) for streaming, path-controllable character motion, directly useful for game/animation prototyping. Docked for unlicensed checkpoints and SMPL-H dependency for meshes.
